qualification.reason: The document is a Request for Quotations (RFQ) issued by the NYS Office of General Services for the procurement of hardware configurations, including submission deadlines, scope, evaluation criteria, and terms and conditions. It is a solicitation for competitive quotes from authorized contractors.

quotes.quote: RFQ Title Aggregate Hardware Buy 20-01 RFQ Number 20-01

Request for Quotations 20-01 
Aggregate Hardware Buy

OGS is seeking competitive quotes from Contract holders of the OGS Group 73600 Award 22802 Information Technology Umbrella Contract – Manufacturer Based (Statewide) (“Manufacturer Umbrella Contract”) for the Lots indicated below.
BASIS FOR AWARD Highest Total Financial Score meeting specified Technical Requirements and Mandatory Pass/Fail Requirements.

OGS is releasing this Request for Quotes (RFQ) for Aggregate Hardware Buy 20-01 (“RFQ 20-01”). The purpose of RFQ 20-01 is to establish an award for each Configuration as set forth in Attachment A - Technical Response.

findings.title: Bid Validity Period
findings.fact: Quotes and pricing must remain valid for at least 120 calendar days from the due date, unless extended by mutual consent.

quotes.quote: Quotes and pricing submitted in response to RFQ 20-01 must remain open and valid for at least one hundred-twenty (120) calendar days from the date that RFQ Submissions are due, unless the time for making an award is extended by mutual consent of OGS and the Contractor.

findings.title: Reseller restrictions
findings.fact: Contractors may use Resellers for order fulfillment, but Resellers are not authorized to receive purchase orders or invoice Authorized Users; Contractor remains solely responsible.

quotes.quote: Contractors are permitted to use Resellers in the fulfillment of orders under any resulting Aggregate Agreement. Contractors must receive payment from Authorized Users directly and must invoice Authorized Users directly. OGS approved Resellers and Sales Agents are not authorized to receive Purchase Orders from Authorized Users or to invoice Authorized Users.

findings.title: OGS Issues Responses to Questions
findings.fact: OGS will issue responses to questions and comments on 11/23/20.

quotes.quote: OGS Issues Responses to Questions and Comments 11/23/20

findings.title: Attachment C Financial Response Distribution
findings.fact: OGS sends out Attachment C – Financial Response on 1/21/21.

quotes.quote: OGS sends out Attachment C – Financial Response, which includes approved technical response 1/21/21

findings.title: Purchase Order Receipt Notification and Advanced Shipping Notice
findings.fact: The awarded contractor must provide a Purchase Order receipt notification to the Authorized User within 5 calendar days of receipt, and an Advanced Shipping Notice upon request 14 calendar days prior to delivery.

quotes.quote: The Awarded Contractor(s) must provide a Purchase Order receipt notification to the Authorized User within five (5) calendar days of receipt of a Purchase Order.
An Advanced Shipping Notice must be provided to Authorized Users upon request fourteen (14) calendar days prior to delivery.

findings.title: Imaging/Loading Services Timelines
findings.fact: For customized factory imaging, the contractor shall provide a test unit within 5 business days of receiving the image, and deliver the remainder of imaged units within 30 calendar days from written approval of the test unit, but not less than 45 days from Purchase Order.

quotes.quote: If an Authorized User requires customized factory imaging, the awarded Contractor(s) shall provide a test unit with the customized image within five (5) business days of receiving the Authorized User’s image.

The Awarded Contractor(s) must deliver the remainder of the imaged units ordered by the Authorized User, within thirty (30) calendar days from the date of Authorized User’s written approval of the test unit.
Notwithstanding the foregoing in this clause the delivery date shall not be required to be less than 45 days from date of Purchase Order.

findings.title: OGS Reserved Rights to Change Schedule Dates
findings.fact: OGS reserves the right to change any of the schedule dates with notification via email to all applicable Manufacturer Umbrella Contractors.

quotes.quote: Change any of the schedule dates with notification via email to all applicable Manufacturer Umbrella Contractors;

findings.title: Additional Products Not Factored into Evaluation
findings.fact: Pricing for Additional Products will not be factored into the evaluation.

quotes.quote: Pricing for any Additional Products will not be factored into the evaluation, but submission of items for review at the time of bid will facilitate the availability of Additional Products for Authorized Users as part of a Configuration at time of award.

findings.title: OGS Reserved Rights in Evaluation
findings.fact: OGS reserves the right to seek clarifications, require corrections, and modify specifications prior to financial evaluation.

quotes.quote: Seek clarifications and revisions of the RFQ response;

Require clarification at any time during the procurement process and/or require correction of arithmetic or other apparent errors for the purpose of assuring a full and complete understanding of a Contractor’s RFQ Responses and/or to determine a Contractor’s compliance with the requirements of the RFQ;

Modify a specification within the Standard Configuration or Required Product categories in Attachment A – Technical Response or Attachment C – Financial Response prior to the Financial Evaluation, upon written notice to Contractors that have submitted a quote.

findings.title: Evaluation of Discount Percentages
findings.fact: Discount percentages for Required Products are evaluated and must be expressed as a single value, not a range.

quotes.quote: A Discount Percentage value cannot be expressed as a range (for example: 10%-20%, or “varies”).

findings.title: Additional Products Discount Application
findings.fact: The same discount percentages bid for Required Product categories apply to Additional Products in their respective categories, and these percentages apply to the Net NYS Contract Price from the Manufacturer Umbrella Contract Price List.

quotes.quote: Contractors shall provide the same awarded discount percentages that applied to the three (3) Required Product categories (Warranty and Services, Components, and Peripherals), to the Additional Products in their respective categories.
For all Additional Products, the discount percentages will apply to the Net NYS Contract Price from the Manufacturer Umbrella Contract Price List.

findings.title: Contractor Website Restrictions
findings.fact: Contractor's dedicated website must not have ordering capability and must only show approved models; conflicts with OGS price lists resolved in favor of OGS.

quotes.quote: The Contractors website shall not have a web-based ordering system with the capability of receiving orders from Authorized Users.
Any conflicts between the OGS-posted price lists and items on a Contractor’s dedicated website shall be resolved in favor of the OGS-posted price list at time of the sale.

findings.title: Agreement Extension to Other Jurisdictions
findings.fact: Agreement pricing may be extended to other states or governmental jurisdictions upon mutual written agreement; New York State reserves right to negotiate additional discounts.

quotes.quote: This Agreement Pricing may be extended to additional States or Governmental jurisdictions upon mutual written agreement between New York State (the lead contracting State) and the Contractor.
New York State reserves the right to negotiate additional discounts based on any increased volume generated by such extensions.

findings.title: Price List Modification
findings.fact: Contractor can modify pricing and products via Appendix 2 and 3; only one modification at a time; pricing can be lowered anytime.

quotes.quote: The Awarded Contractor is authorized to provide the Standard Configuration(s), Required Products, and Additional Products initially awarded in the Aggregate Hardware Buy 20-01 Agreement. Products included under the Agreement can be modified through the processes described in RFQ 20-01, Appendix 2 – Agreement Price List Modification Procedures and utilizing RFQ 20-01, Appendix 3 - Pricing Modification Form.
In order to expedite processing of an Agreement Modification, only one Agreement Modification request can be submitted at a time.
All Product pricing on the Contractor’s Aggregate Buy 20-01 Price List can be lowered at any time throughout the term of the Agreement and any extensions.

findings.title: Adding Additional Products
findings.fact: Additional products must first be approved on Manufacturer Umbrella Contract; new price must be <= net NYS contract price; discount applied.

quotes.quote: After Agreement award, in order for Products to be added to the Additional Products pricing category under the Agreement, Products must first be approved on the Manufacturer Umbrella Contract in accordance with the Manufacturer Umbrella Contract’s Appendix C – Contract Modification Procedure.

The new Additional Product price, as entered in the Proposed Aggregate Agreement Price column on the RFQ 20-01, Appendix 3 – Pricing Modification Form, must be equal to or less than the net NYS Contract price for this Product as listed on the Manufacturer Umbrella Price List.

findings.title: Replacement of Products
findings.fact: Replacement products must be equal or greater spec, same or lower price; 60 days notice for EOL; OGS determines compliance.

quotes.quote: If a Product in the awarded Standard Configurations and/or Required Products becomes incompatible, obsolete or unavailable, a replacement Product of equal or greater specification than the original Product offered in the Standard Configurations and/or Required Products must first be submitted for OGS approval by completing the modification process outlined in Appendix 2 – Price List Modification Procedures.
The replacement Product must be offered on the Aggregate Agreement Price List at the same or lower Aggregate Hardware Buy 20-01 Agreement pricing as the Product it is replacing.
Contractor must provide advance notification of no less than sixty (60) calendar days for EOL Products in order for OGS to process modifications for Product substitutions in a timely manner.

findings.title: Invoicing Requirements
findings.fact: Invoices must include specific items such as contract number, RFQ number, product details, and aggregate buy price.

quotes.quote: All Invoices shall at a minimum, include the items listed below and any additional information identified in the Authorized User Purchase Order and resulting Authorized User Agreement:

• Manufacturer Umbrella Contract Number: PMXXXXX • RFQ Number: 20-01 • RFQ Title: Aggregate Hardware Buy 20-01 • Awarded Contractor Name • NYS Vendor ID • Manufacturer Part Number (SKU) • Product Name • Product Description • Quantity • Aggregate Buy Price for each Product • Specific designation of special price(s) which may be better than the Aggregate Buy Price • Invoice Total • Standard Configuration Name

findings.title: Replacement Contractor Pricing Constraints
findings.fact: If OGS terminates the Agreement and awards to the next highest scoring contractor, that new awardee cannot increase component prices for Standard Configurations, Required Products, or decrease percentage discounts on Additional Products.

quotes.quote: Under no circumstances will the new awardee be permitted to increase its component prices for Standard Configurations, the prices of the Required Products or decrease the percentage discounts on Additional Products that were originally bid.

findings.title: Only Lot 2 Hardware Contractors Eligible
findings.fact: RFQ 20-01 is only distributed to Contractors holding an award for Lot 2 – Hardware on the Manufacturer Umbrella Contract. Quotes will only be accepted from Lot 2 Contractors; Resellers are not eligible and will be disqualified.
findings.business_implication: This RFQ is exclusively for manufacturers with an existing Lot 2 Hardware contract. Resellers or non-Lot 2 contractors cannot participate, and any such bid will be rejected.
findings.action_recommendation: Confirm your company's eligibility as a Lot 2 Hardware contractor before investing time in preparing a response. If you are a reseller, do not submit a bid.

quotes.quote: Quotes from Resellers will not be accepted. Contractors must have an award for Lot 2 to bid on this RFQ.

RFQ 20-01 is only being distributed to Contractors holding an award for Lot 2 – Hardware on the Manufacturer Umbrella Contract (“Contractors”). Quotes under RFQ 20-01 will only be accepted from Lot 2 Contractors on the Manufacturer Umbrella Contract; Resellers are not eligible to respond and any bids from a Reseller will be disqualified.

findings.title: Products Must Be on Lot 2 Price List
findings.fact: All products proposed must be on the Contractor's Lot 2 - Hardware price list at the time of the RFQ Submission due date.
findings.business_implication: Only products already listed on your Lot 2 Hardware price list can be offered. This ensures pricing and availability are pre-approved, but may limit your ability to propose new or updated products.
findings.action_recommendation: Review your current Lot 2 price list to ensure all proposed products are included. If any product is missing, update your price list before the submission deadline.

quotes.quote: All Products proposed as part of the Standard Configuration and Products proposed for Required Products, as well as any Additional Products, must be on the Contractor's Lot 2 - Hardware price list at the time of the RFQ Submission due date.

findings.title: Eligibility restricted to Manufacturer Umbrella Contract holders
findings.fact: Only Contractors holding a Manufacturer Umbrella Contract with OGS are eligible to respond to this RFQ.
findings.business_implication: This RFQ is only open to manufacturers who already have an OGS Manufacturer Umbrella Contract. This limits competition to established vendors and ensures compliance with existing terms.
findings.action_recommendation: Verify that your company holds a valid Manufacturer Umbrella Contract with OGS. If not, you cannot bid; consider partnering with an eligible manufacturer if appropriate.

quotes.quote: The terms and conditions of the Contractor’s Manufacturer Umbrella Contract including any Amendments and the additional terms and conditions set forth in this RFQ 20-01 Section 7 - Terms and Conditions govern the resulting award under RFQ 20-01.
This Page is to be Completed By the Manufacturer Responding to the RFQ

findings.title: Exclusion of entities on US Customs and Border Patrol lists
findings.fact: OGS will not accept a bid from a Contractor or a product containing products made by an entity on any of the lists maintained by the US Customs and Border Patrol.
findings.business_implication: Bids involving entities on US Customs and Border Patrol restricted lists will be rejected. This could affect your supply chain and product availability.
findings.action_recommendation: Screen your company and all suppliers against the US Customs and Border Patrol lists. If any entity is listed, remove affected products from your bid or find alternative suppliers.

quotes.quote: OGS will not accept a bid from a Contractor, or a Contractor product that contains products made by an entity on any of the lists maintained by the US Customs and Border Patrol at the link set out below.

findings.title: EPEAT certification required for certain products
findings.fact: Desktops, laptops, and computer monitors must have EPEAT Silver certification at time of award; Interactive Displays must have EPEAT Bronze.
findings.business_implication: Products must meet specific environmental standards. Failure to meet these certifications could disqualify your bid or delay award.
findings.action_recommendation: Ensure all proposed desktops, laptops, and monitors have EPEAT Silver certification, and interactive displays have EPEAT Bronze. Verify certifications before submission.

quotes.quote: Desktops, laptops, and computer monitors provided under this Agreement are required to have achieved a minimum certification of EPEAT Silver at the time of award, apart from the Products included in the Interactive Displays Configuration. Interactive Displays classes will be required to meet a minimum certification of EPEAT Bronze at the time of award.

findings.title: Mandatory eMarketplace participation for award
findings.fact: Contractors with winning bids must agree to participate in the eMarketplace to receive an award.
findings.business_implication: This is a mandatory condition for award; failure to agree will disqualify the bidder even if they have the winning bid. It also implies additional operational setup and potential costs for catalog management, though no fees are required for basic participation.
findings.action_recommendation: Ensure that the organization is prepared to participate in the NYS eMarketplace. Review the eMarketplace requirements and plan for catalog setup and maintenance. Confirm internal capability to comply with this condition before bidding.

quotes.quote: The Contractor with the winning bid for each Configuration may not receive an award until Contractor agrees to participate in the eMarketplace.

findings.title: RFQ Submission Deadline
findings.fact: RFQ Submissions are due by 12/9/20 at 11:00am EST.
findings.business_implication: This is a critical deadline. Missing it will result in automatic disqualification. The submission includes multiple attachments, so adequate time must be allocated for preparation.
findings.action_recommendation: Mark the deadline on calendars and set internal reminders. Ensure all required documents (Attachment A, Attachment D, Manufacturer Information Page) are completed and submitted well before the deadline. Consider submitting early to avoid last-minute issues.

quotes.quote: RFQ Submission Due Submission Includes: • Attachment A – Technical Response • Attachment D – Issue Escalation Plan • Manufacturer Information Page (Last page of this Document) 12/9/20 11:00am EST

findings.title: Questions and Comments Due Date
findings.fact: Attachment B - Contractor Questions and Comments are due by 11/13/20 at 5:00pm EST.
findings.business_implication: This is the only opportunity to seek clarification on the RFQ. Missing this deadline means any ambiguities will remain unresolved, potentially affecting the bid quality.
findings.action_recommendation: Review the RFQ thoroughly and submit any questions or comments via email to the specified address before the deadline. Ensure the subject line is correct and that the submission is complete.

quotes.quote: Attachment B - Contractor Questions and Comments Due 11/13/20 5:00pm EST

findings.title: Attachment C Financial Response Return Deadline
findings.fact: Contractors must return completed Attachment C – Financial Response by 1/28/21 at 11:00am EST.
findings.business_implication: This is a critical deadline for the financial proposal. Missing it will result in disqualification. The financial response is likely a key factor in award decisions.
findings.action_recommendation: Plan to receive and complete Attachment C promptly after it is sent on 1/21/21. Ensure all financial data is accurate and submitted before the deadline. Consider preparing financial information in advance to expedite the process.

quotes.quote: Contractor returns completed Attachment C – Financial Response 1/28/21 11:00am EST

findings.title: Delivery Period and Extensions
findings.fact: The awarded contractor shall deliver units within 45 calendar days of receipt of a Purchase Order, with possible extension to 60 calendar days upon request, and beyond 60 days only with OGS approval under certain conditions.
findings.business_implication: This sets strict delivery performance expectations. Failure to meet the 45-day requirement may lead to penalties or loss of future business. Extensions are possible but require approval and are subject to conditions.
findings.action_recommendation: Assess internal supply chain capabilities to meet the 45-day delivery requirement. If there is risk of delay, plan to request extensions promptly and document reasons. Understand the conditions for OGS approval for delays beyond 60 days and ensure compliance.

quotes.quote: The Awarded Contractor(s) shall deliver the units ordered by an Authorized User within forty-five (45) calendar days of receipt of a Purchase Order unless either the Authorized User or OGS grants an extension of time as provided below.

If upon receipt of a Purchase Order the Awarded Contractor determines it cannot meet the 45 calendar day delivery period the Awarded Contractor may submit a written request to the Authorized User to extend the required Product delivery period to up to sixty (60) calendar days.

If an Authorized User wants to extend the delivery period beyond sixty (60) calendar days, the Authorized User may submit a written request to extend the Product delivery period beyond sixty (60) calendar days to OGS for its approval.

findings.title: EOL Notification Deadlines
findings.fact: OGS must receive no less than 60 calendar days' notice for EOL Additional Products, EOL Replacement Products, and EOL Standard Configurations, and no less than 30 calendar days prior to a Standard Configuration becoming obsolete for a substitute submission.
findings.business_implication: The bidder must manage product lifecycles proactively to avoid contract non-compliance and potential penalties. Missing these deadlines could result in inability to replace products, leading to loss of revenue and customer dissatisfaction.
findings.action_recommendation: Implement a robust product lifecycle management process to track EOL dates and ensure timely notifications to OGS. Set internal alerts well in advance (e.g., 90 days) to allow for preparation and submission of required notices.

quotes.quote: OGS must receive no less than 60 calendar days’ notice for EOL Additional Products.
OGS must receive no less than sixty (60) calendar days’ notice for EOL Products.
OGS must receive notification no less than 60 calendar days before a Standard Configuration model becomes EOL.

No less than 30 calendar days prior to the awarded Standard Configuration becoming obsolete or unavailable for purchase by Authorized Users, a substitute Standard Configuration with specifications that meet or exceed the specifications of the original offered Standard Configuration must be submitted for OGS approval by completing the modification process outlined in Appendix 2 – Price List Modification Procedures.

findings.title: Basis for Award
findings.fact: Awards will be made to the responsive and responsible Contractor(s) with the highest Total Financial Score per Configuration that meets all specified technical requirements. The same awardee can be awarded multiple Configurations.
findings.business_implication: The bidder's pricing strategy is critical, as the award is based on the highest Total Financial Score (lowest cost) per configuration. Winning multiple configurations is possible, offering potential for increased revenue but also requiring competitive pricing across all configurations.
findings.action_recommendation: Develop a pricing strategy that is aggressive yet sustainable for each configuration. Analyze competitors and market rates to ensure the bid is competitive while maintaining profitability. Consider bundling or cross-subsidization if allowed.

quotes.quote: Awards will be made to the responsive and responsible Contractor(s) with the highest Total Financial Score per Configuration that meets all the specified technical requirements. The same awardee can be awarded multiple Configurations.

findings.title: Stage 1 Administrative Review
findings.fact: Stage 1 reviews Attachment A, Attachment D, and Manufacturer Information page for completeness. Alterations to documents are prohibited and may result in rejection.
findings.business_implication: Any unauthorized modifications to the provided templates can lead to immediate disqualification, wasting all effort and resources invested in the bid. Strict adherence to document formats is essential.
findings.action_recommendation: Ensure all personnel involved in bid preparation are trained on the document requirements. Use version control and review processes to verify that no alterations are made. Double-check that all required fields are completed before submission.

quotes.quote: The submitted Attachment A – Technical Response, Attachment D – Issue Escalation Plan, and the Manufacturer Information page (last page of this document) will be reviewed for completeness. The addition or deletion of worksheets, columns, unlocking the document, rewriting formulas, or similar alterations to any document is prohibited. OGS reserves the right to reject any Contractor Submission or portion(s) thereof determined to have been altered/modified by the Contractor from the original format. Failure to provide fully completed documents may result in rejection of the RFQ Response without further review.

findings.title: Stage 2 Technical Evaluation
findings.fact: Attachment A is compared to Standard Configuration and Required Products requirements. SKUs must be on the Contractor's approved Manufacturer Umbrella Contract Price List. Configurations with SKUs not on the price list may not proceed.
findings.business_implication: The bidder must ensure that all proposed SKUs are already on the Manufacturer Umbrella Contract Price List before submission. Any missing SKUs could cause the entire configuration to be disqualified, losing potential awards.
findings.action_recommendation: Before submission, cross-check every SKU in Attachment A against the approved Manufacturer Umbrella Contract Price List. If any SKU is missing, initiate a contract modification request well in advance to have it added. Prioritize this for all configurations intended to be bid.

quotes.quote: Submitted Attachment A – Technical Response will be compared to Standard Configuration and Required Products requirements. All proposed SKUs for proposed products offered in Attachment A – Technical Response must be on the Contractor’s approved Manufacturer Umbrella Contract Price List. Any Configuration that contains a SKU that is not included on the Manufacturer’s Umbrella Contract Price List may not proceed further in the evaluation process.

findings.title: Stage 3 Financial Evaluation
findings.fact: Only Contractors whose Standard Configuration specifications and Required Products pass review proceed to financial evaluation. Attachment C is used for pricing evaluation.
findings.business_implication: The bidder must first pass the technical evaluation to be considered for the financial evaluation. This means technical compliance is a prerequisite, and pricing is only considered for technically compliant bids.
findings.action_recommendation: Focus on ensuring technical compliance in Attachment A to pass Stage 2. Once technical compliance is assured, prepare Attachment C with competitive pricing. Note that Attachment C is generated from Attachment A, so accuracy in Attachment A is crucial.

quotes.quote: Only Contractors whose Standard Configuration specifications and Required Products pass review, as determined by OGS, will proceed to the evaluation of Attachment C – Financial Response for those specific Configurations. For those Contractors who have been determined to have passed the Technical Evaluation, their Attachment A - Technical Response will be used to create the Attachment C – Financial Response and be provided to the Contractor in order to complete and submit. The proposed pricing on Attachment C – Financial Response will then be used in the Financial Evaluation.

findings.title: Mandatory Products and Evaluation Components
findings.fact: All components within Standard Configuration and Required Products are mandatory. Failure to complete required fields may result in rejection. Pricing on Attachment C must be equal to or better than Manufacturer Umbrella Contract pricing.
findings.business_implication: The bidder must ensure that all mandatory components are included and all required fields in Attachments A and C are fully completed to avoid disqualification. Additionally, pricing must be at or below the Manufacturer Umbrella Contract pricing, which may limit the bidder's ability to offer competitive pricing.
findings.action_recommendation: Thoroughly review the RFQ requirements and ensure all mandatory components are included in the bid. Double-check that all required fields in Attachments A and C are completed accurately. Verify that all proposed pricing is equal to or better than the Manufacturer Umbrella Contract pricing to ensure compliance.

quotes.quote: ALL COMPONENTS WITHIN THE STANDARD CONFIGURATION AND ITS REQUIRED PRODUCTS ARE MANDATORY. Failure to complete all required fields in Attachment A – Technical Response or Attachment C – Financial Response may result in rejection of the RFQ Response without further review.
All pricing offered on Attachment C - Financial Response must be equal to or better than the pricing offered for that SKU on the Contractor's Manufacturer Umbrella Contract.

findings.title: Evaluation of Required Products and Discounts
findings.fact: Required Products are designated for evaluation purposes, and the discount percentages bid on Required Products will be factored into the final Quote price for evaluation.
findings.business_implication: The bidder's discount percentages on Required Products directly impact the evaluation score, as they are factored into the final quote price. Aggressive discounts on Required Products can improve the bidder's competitive position.
findings.action_recommendation: Strategically set discount percentages for Required Products to be as aggressive as possible while maintaining profitability, as these discounts will be used in the financial evaluation and can significantly influence the award decision.

quotes.quote: For evaluation purposes, specific Products have been designated as Required Products.
Contractors are encouraged to aggressively discount their pricing for their Required Products, as the pricing will be factored in the final Quote price for evaluation.

findings.title: Required Products Discount Percentage
findings.fact: Contractors must bid a discount percentage for each Required Product category, and the discount on the selected product applies to all Additional Products in the same category. Discount percentages may be increased but not decreased during the term.
findings.business_implication: The bidder must carefully set discount percentages for Required Products, as these discounts will apply to all Additional Products in the same category, potentially affecting profitability across a wide range of items. Once set, discounts cannot be decreased during the contract term, so the bidder must ensure the discounts are sustainable.
findings.action_recommendation: Analyze the product categories and estimate the potential volume of Additional Products to set discount percentages that are competitive yet sustainable. Ensure that the discount percentages are set at a level that can be maintained for the contract duration, as they cannot be reduced later.

quotes.quote: For Required Products, Contractors must bid a discount percentage on the item that has been selected for each category (e.g., a 3-button mouse for Peripherals).
The discount that is bid on the single Product shall apply to all Additional Products in the same Required Product category, as described in Section 7.3.5 – Additional Product Discount.
The discount percentages may be increased, but not decreased during the term of the Agreement and any extensions.

findings.title: Financial Evaluation Weighting
findings.fact: The Financial Response is 100% of the evaluation, with points allocated as: Standard Configuration 50 points, Required Products (Warranty/Services 15, Components 30, Peripherals 5).
findings.business_implication: The bidder's pricing strategy is the sole determinant of the award, with the Standard Configuration and Required Products carrying specific weights. The bidder must focus on offering the lowest total cost for the Standard Configuration and Required Products to maximize the financial score.
findings.action_recommendation: Develop a competitive pricing strategy that optimizes the total cost for the Standard Configuration and Required Products, as these are the only factors in the evaluation. Consider aggressive pricing on Required Products, especially Components (30 points) and Warranty/Services (15 points), to gain a competitive edge.

quotes.quote: Financial Response : 100%

Total Financial Score is based on lowest cost and the points are weighted as follows: • Standard Configuration - 50 points • Required Products o Warranty/Services - 15 points o Components - 30 points o Peripherals - 5 points

findings.title: Estimated Spend and Quantity
findings.fact: The estimated dollar value of the aggregated award is approximately $40 million, but there is no guarantee of volume or dollar value to be purchased.
findings.business_implication: While the potential contract value is significant, the bidder cannot rely on the estimated $40 million as a guaranteed revenue stream. The actual volume and dollar value of purchases may vary substantially, so the bidder should not overcommit resources based on the estimate.
findings.action_recommendation: Prepare a bid that is financially viable even if actual purchases are lower than estimated. Avoid making investments or commitments that depend on the full $40 million materializing. Consider the potential for higher volumes if pricing is competitive, but plan for uncertainty.

quotes.quote: The estimated dollar value of the aggregated award of the fourteen (14) Standard Configurations in this RFQ, based on historical purchases under previous awards, is approximately $40 million.
There is no guarantee of volume to be purchased
There is no guarantee of dollar value to be purchased

findings.title: eMarketplace Participation
findings.fact: Contractors awarded a Configuration must provide a hosted or punch-out catalog via NYS eMarketplace; there are no fees for mandatory participation, but optional ERP integration may incur fees.
findings.business_implication: The bidder must be prepared to set up and maintain an eMarketplace catalog, which may require additional resources and costs for ERP integration if desired. Failure to comply could jeopardize the award.
findings.action_recommendation: Plan for eMarketplace catalog setup and consider the costs and benefits of ERP integration. Ensure the catalog is accurate and up-to-date to avoid compliance issues.

quotes.quote: Contractors that are awarded a Configuration under the Aggregate Agreement should provide a “hosted” or “punch-out” catalog that is available to Authorized Users via the NYS eMarketplace.

There are no fees required for a Contractor’s mandatory participation in the catalog site development or management. However, Contractors who wish to integrate their ERP system with the NYS eMarketplace can do so for an additional fee.

findings.title: Agreement Term and Extensions
findings.fact: Initial term is one year, with OGS option to extend up to one additional year, and possible short-term extension up to 3 months (or 6 with contractor concurrence).
findings.business_implication: The contract duration is uncertain and could extend up to 2.5 years, affecting resource planning and pricing stability. The bidder must be prepared for potential extensions.
findings.action_recommendation: Factor in the possibility of extensions when pricing and planning resources. Be prepared to continue performance if OGS exercises its extension options.

quotes.quote: The term of the Aggregate Hardware Buy 20-01 Agreement shall be one (1) year.

OGS reserves the right, at its sole discretion, to extend all or some Configurations of the Aggregate Hardware Buy 20-01 Agreement for a period up to an additional one (1) year upon written notice to the Contractor.

In the event a replacement Agreement has not been issued, any Agreement let and awarded hereunder by the State, may be extended unilaterally by the State for an additional period of up to three (3) months upon notice to the Awarded Contractor with the same terms and conditions as the original Agreement including, but not limited to, prices and delivery requirements. With the concurrence of the Awarded Contractor, the extension may be for a period of up to six (6) months in lieu of three (3) months.

findings.title: Reseller Participation
findings.fact: Contractors may use Resellers for fulfillment, but must receive payment and invoice directly; Resellers cannot receive POs or invoice; Contractor remains responsible.
findings.business_implication: The bidder can leverage resellers for fulfillment but must maintain direct billing and payment relationships with customers. The bidder bears full responsibility for reseller actions, so careful oversight is needed.
findings.action_recommendation: If using resellers, establish clear contracts and monitoring mechanisms to ensure compliance. Ensure all invoicing and payment flows go through the bidder to avoid contractual breaches.

quotes.quote: Contractors are permitted to use Resellers in the fulfillment of orders under any resulting Aggregate Agreement.

Contractors must receive payment from Authorized Users directly and must invoice Authorized Users directly. OGS approved Resellers and Sales Agents are not authorized to receive Purchase Orders from Authorized Users or to invoice Authorized Users.

Contractors remain wholly and solely responsible for the actions of the Resellers acting on their behalf as part of the aggregate purchase, as well as the performance of all Products, and conformity with the Manufacturer Umbrella Contract and any agreement resulting from this RFQ.

findings.title: Administrative Fee Rate and Payment Terms
findings.fact: The awarded Contractor(s) are required to pay an Administrative Fee of 0.50% for all sales generated from this Aggregate Hardware Buy 20-01 Agreement, due quarterly in arrears.
findings.business_implication: The bidder must account for the 0.50% administrative fee in pricing and cash flow planning. Quarterly payments are required, so financial systems must be set up to track and remit fees accurately.
findings.action_recommendation: Incorporate the administrative fee into pricing models and establish internal processes for accurate sales reporting and timely fee payments to avoid penalties.

quotes.quote: The awarded Contractor(s) are required to pay an Administrative Fee in the amount of point five percent (0.50%) for all sales generated from this Aggregate Hardware Buy 20-01 Agreement.
Payments will be due quarterly in arrears. The due date for each payment will be fifteen (15) calendar days following the end of the quarter.

findings.title: Fiscal Audit and Underpayment Penalties
findings.fact: If an audit reveals underpayment of Administrative Fees by more than 5%, Contractor must pay audit costs or three times the discrepancy, whichever is higher.
findings.business_implication: The bidder faces significant financial penalties if administrative fees are underpaid by more than 5% due to inaccurate reporting. This underscores the need for meticulous sales tracking and reporting.
findings.action_recommendation: Implement robust sales reporting and internal audit controls to ensure accurate fee calculations. Regularly reconcile sales data to avoid underpayment and potential penalties.

quotes.quote: If, as a result of any such audit, Administrative Fees are determined to have been underpaid by more than five percent (5%) for the period audited, Contractor shall pay the costs of such audit or three times the discrepancy, whichever is higher.

findings.title: Contractor Liability for Replacement Components
findings.fact: If replacement components are incompatible with RFQ 20-01 peripherals, the Contractor is responsible for replacement of both the component and the peripheral.
findings.business_implication: The bidder bears the financial risk of replacing both the component and the peripheral if the replacement component is incompatible. This could lead to significant unexpected costs if compatibility issues arise.
findings.action_recommendation: Ensure thorough compatibility testing of all replacement components with existing peripherals before offering them. Maintain a process to verify compatibility and consider including warranty or indemnification clauses to mitigate this risk.

quotes.quote: Replacement components within the Aggregate Hardware Buy RFQ 20-01 must be compatible with RFQ 20-01 peripherals or the Contractor will be responsible for replacement of both the component and the peripheral.

findings.title: Contractor Liability for EOL Products
findings.fact: All EOL products purchased by Authorized Users must remain under warranty or be replaceable at no additional charge to the Authorized Users.
findings.business_implication: The bidder must ensure that end-of-life products continue to be supported or replaced at no extra cost to customers, which could create ongoing financial obligations and affect profitability.
findings.action_recommendation: Plan for end-of-life product lifecycle management, including setting aside reserves or negotiating extended warranties with manufacturers. Clearly communicate EOL policies to customers and ensure compliance with warranty obligations.

quotes.quote: All EOL Additional Products purchased by Authorized Users must remained under warranty or be replaceable at no additional charge to the Authorized Users.
All EOL Replacement Products purchased by Authorized Users must remain under warranty or be replaceable at no additional charge to the Authorized Users.
All EOL Standard Configurations purchased by Authorized Users must remain under warranty or be replaceable at no additional charge to the Authorized Users.

findings.title: Contractor Liability for Extended Agreement Participants
findings.fact: When the Agreement is extended to other states or jurisdictions, those entities are solely responsible for liability and performance, and Contractor agrees to hold them solely responsible.
findings.business_implication: The bidder is protected from liability for extended entities, but must ensure that these entities are capable of fulfilling their obligations. This could affect the bidder's reputation if extended entities fail to perform.
findings.action_recommendation: Conduct due diligence on any entities that may be extended under the agreement. Clearly document the responsibilities and liabilities of each party to avoid ambiguity and potential disputes.

quotes.quote: In the event that this Agreement is so extended, such other authorized entities shall be solely responsible for liability and performance under the Agreement and Contractor agrees to hold them solely responsible for such liability and performance.

findings.title: Term and Extension Provisions
findings.fact: The Aggregate Hardware Buy 20-01 Agreement has a one-year term, with OGS reserving the right to extend for up to an additional one year, and a short-term extension provision allowing unilateral extension for up to three months (or six months with contractor concurrence) if a replacement agreement has not been issued.
findings.business_implication: The bidder must be prepared for potential extensions beyond the initial term, which could affect resource allocation and pricing stability. The unilateral extension clause gives OGS flexibility, potentially extending the contract without the bidder's consent.
findings.action_recommendation: Plan for potential extensions by ensuring pricing and terms remain viable for up to two years. Monitor contract renewal timelines and maintain open communication with OGS regarding extension intentions.

quotes.quote: The term of the Aggregate Hardware Buy 20-01 Agreement shall be one (1) year. The term shall not commence until OGS execution and posting of the final executed documents to the Awarded Contractor(s). OGS reserves the right, at its sole discretion, to extend all or some Configurations of the Aggregate Hardware Buy 20-01 Agreement for a period up to an additional one (1) year upon written notice to the Contractor.

OGS reserves the right to seek an additional short-term extension for the Aggregate Hardware Buy 20-01 Agreement in accordance with Manufacturer Umbrella Contract, Section 5, Short Term Extension: In the event a replacement Agreement has not been issued, any Agreement let and awarded hereunder by the State, may be extended unilaterally by the State for an additional period of up to three (3) months upon notice to the Awarded Contractor with the same terms and conditions as the original Agreement including, but not limited to, prices and delivery requirements. With the concurrence of the Awarded Contractor, the extension may be for a period of up to six (6) months in lieu of three (3) months. However, this extension terminates should the replacement Agreement be issued in the interim.

findings.title: Termination for Delivery Delays
findings.fact: OGS reserves the right to terminate the Agreement in whole or in part if it becomes aware of multiple incidents of delays in delivery.
findings.business_implication: The bidder faces the risk of contract termination if delivery delays occur repeatedly, which could result in loss of revenue and damage to reputation.
findings.action_recommendation: Implement robust supply chain management and delivery tracking systems to minimize delays. Maintain clear communication with OGS regarding any potential delays and proactively address issues to avoid termination.

quotes.quote: If OGS becomes aware of multiple incidents of delays in delivery, OGS reserves the right to terminate the Agreement in whole or in part.

findings.title: Termination for Failure to Submit Accurate Sales Reports
findings.fact: Failure to submit accurate sales reports on a timely basis may result in termination of the Contractor’s Manufacturer Umbrella Contract in whole or in part and activation of the Replacement Contractor clause.
findings.business_implication: This clause poses a significant risk to the bidder's contract. Inaccurate or late sales reports can lead to termination of the entire Manufacturer Umbrella Contract, not just the Aggregate Hardware Buy agreement, and could result in the contract being awarded to a competitor. This could severely impact revenue and market position.
findings.action_recommendation: Implement robust internal controls and a dedicated team to ensure sales reports are accurate and submitted on time. Set up automated reminders and a review process to double-check data before submission. Consider investing in reporting software to streamline the process and minimize errors.

quotes.quote: Failure to submit accurate reports on a timely basis may result in termination of the Contractor’s Manufacturer Umbrella Contract in whole or in part and activation 7.23 Replacement Contractor.

findings.title: Termination for Audit Underpayments
findings.fact: Failure to make payments for audit discrepancies or repeated errors on subsequent audits may lead to termination of this Agreement in whole or in part, after which OGS reserves the right to award to the second-place contractor.
findings.business_implication: This clause exposes the bidder to financial penalties and potential contract termination. If an audit reveals underpayment of administrative fees by more than 5%, the bidder must pay the audit costs or three times the discrepancy, whichever is higher. Repeated errors could lead to termination and loss of the contract to a competitor.
findings.action_recommendation: Maintain meticulous records of all sales and administrative fee calculations. Conduct internal audits regularly to ensure accuracy and compliance. If discrepancies are found, address them immediately and implement corrective actions to prevent recurrence. Establish a clear process for responding to audit findings and making timely payments.

quotes.quote: Failure to make such payments or repeated errors on subsequent audits may result in the scheduling of a responsibility meeting in relation to Contractor’s Manufacturer Umbrella Contract, and may lead to termination of this Agreement in whole or in part, after which OGS reserves the right to award to the second-place contractor.
